 Manchester Animation Festival will stop accepting films made with generative AI starting with its 2027 edition. The U.K. festival announced the change Friday as it revealed the winners of its 2026 competition, posted below.
 Festival director Steve Henderson explained the decision in a release, saying:
 After a whirlwind week celebrating the international animation community with screenings, panels, masterclasses and more, our awards are a wonderful way to reflect on the skills and talent we champion at MAF. As we open our call for entries for MAF 2027 we wanted to stand by the creatives that make animation the incredible, human artform that it is. Our new Gen AI policy puts artists first and continues our mission to showcase the very best animation has to offer making it clear for audiences and artists where MAF stands on Gen AI.
 At Thursday’s awards ceremony, Phuong Mai Nguyen’s In Waves , Netflix’s first major pickup at this year’s Cannes, took the top feature prize, with a special mention going to Kōhei Kadowaki’s anime standout We Are Aliens . Mamuka Tkeshelashvili’s When the Sea Was Calm won the Oscar-qualifying short film award, while Leto Meade and Jonathan Rockefeller’s A Little Death was named best British short. Antonin Niclass’ Into the Forest took the audience award and earned a special mention in the children’s competition.
 The five-day festival drew nearly 12,000 admissions, its highest total to date. Manchester Animation Festival returns November 14–18, 2027.
